title: Delay before prisoner found dead, inquest hears
article: A 55-year-old crack addict who died while in police custody lay motionless on her cell floor for 30 minutes before anyone noticed she was in distress, a coroner's inquest heard Monday.

Judy Sanita suffered from "significant health problems" including heart and liver disease and was addressing her crack addiction through a methadone program before she encountered Toronto Police June 23, 2008, counsel to the coroner Lorraine Cavion told jurors in her opening address Monday.

Sanita, a widow with an adult son, had consumed methadone and cocaine before selling crack cocaine to an undercover cop in Stanley Park at 8:45 p.m. on June 23, but she denied having consumed any illicit drugs when questioned at 14 Division following her arrest, court heard.
An autopsy would later show she died from complications of cardiac arrest associated with cocaine.
Four officers testified they noticed nothing to indicate she had consumed drugs and had no concerns about her health.
A video from the station showed a seemingly coherent Sanita answering an officer's questions in a low, raspy voice.
Asked whether she had consumed any drugs, she replied, "Methadone."
Asked if she had any medical conditions: "Cancer patient."
At one point mentioned only in Cavion's opening address, Sanita did say that she "just doesn't feel good," Cavion said.
While Sanita was in her cell, "there was an expectation" that she would be checked on "periodically," Cavion said.

"Two hours later, when two officers approached Ms. Sanita because they wanted to talk to her about an investigation, they found her laying on the cell floor, unresponsive and with a very faint pulse," Cavion said.

After initially laying on her cell bunk, the unsupervised Sanita was captured on video "agitated, moving about as if in discomfort or pain" for about 30 minutes, followed by about 30 minutes during which she lay still on the cell floor, Cavion said. "None of this appears to have been observed."
Officers performed CPR until paramedics arrived. Sanita remained unconscious until she was pronounced dead at Mount Sinai Hospital at 10:03 p.m. on June 24, Cavion said.

Forensic pathologist Dr. David Chiasson testified there was "a pretty significant period of time" between Sanita's heart stopping and starting up again, making the impact on her brain "more significant."
The jury is forbidden from pointing blame, but can make recommendations aimed at preventing similar deaths.
